title: Superfluidity without charge order in the attractive Hubbard model on the kagome lattice
authors: Xiaodong Jin, Yingping Mou, Rubem Mondaini
abstract: Using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we study the zero-temperature attractive Hubbard model on the kagome lattice at various relevant electronic fillings. The low-energy physics at $2/3$-density is influenced by the Dirac point at the Fermi energy, wherein we unveil a superfluid transition at a critical attractive interaction $U_c/t=-4.58(3)$, which belongs to the chiral-XY universality class. This U(1) symmetry-breaking is not accompanied by charge order, even for substantially large interaction strengths, in a regime where a description in terms of hardcore bosons becomes increasingly suitable. An investigation of the latter shows that charge ordering at $1/3$-filling only occurs at interaction strengths much larger than those corresponding to the mapping to the original fermionic model. Additionally, for densities exhibiting van Hove singularities in the non-interacting density of states, our results show that any attractive interaction gives rise to superfluidity, yet again without charge ordering, contrary to recent studies employing mean-field theory.
summary: This work uses quantum Monte Carlo simulations to study the attractive Hubbard model on the kagome lattice. The primary finding is the existence of a superfluid phase transition characterized by chiral-XY criticality that occurs without any accompanying charge density wave order. This challenges mean-field predictions and highlights the role of geometric frustration in stabilizing pure superconducting behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of superfluidity in the attractive Hubbard model on the kagome lattice while simultaneously demonstrating that this pairing transition occurs without any accompanying charge order.
main_result: A superfluid transition is found at a critical interaction $U_c/t = -4.58(3)$ belonging to the chiral-XY universality class, and this superconductivity persists even for large interactions where mean-field theory might predict charge ordering.
method: The research employs auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis to probe the ground state properties across different electronic fillings.
model_or_system: The system is the attractive Hubbard model defined on the geometrically frustrated kagome lattice. The Hamiltonian includes hopping ($t$) and an attractive on-site interaction ($U$).
key_observables: Superfluid order parameter ($	ext{Ps}$), single-particle gap ($\Delta_{sp}$), density correlation functions ($C_n(r)$, $S_n(\mathbf{q})$), and local derivatives of kinetic energy and double occupancy.
important_parameters: Critical attractive interaction ratio ($U_c/t$), electronic filling ($ho=2/3$ for Dirac point, $ho=1/2$, $ho=5/6$ near van Hove singularities).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the applicability of QMC simulations and comparisons with theoretical expectations from mean-field theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the noninteracting band structure showing relevant fillings, and subsequent figures show finite-size scaling collapses of the superfluid order parameter ($\Delta_s$) near the critical point, alongside plots tracking local correlation changes across the transition.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system by first establishing the model and methods (QMC/scaling), then focusing on specific fillings like $ho=2/3$ to find the chiral-XY transition. It contrasts these findings with mean-field predictions and uses local observables ($\partial D/\partial|U|/t$) as secondary confirmation of the phase boundary.
why_interesting: The finding that superfluidity can be robustly established without charge order in a geometrically frustrated lattice like kagome is highly relevant for understanding unconventional superconductivity mechanisms beyond simple mean-field treatments, which often predict coexisting CDW and SC states.
